name: Federal Fed-Flash
note: same camera — the American Federal Mfg & Engineering 'Fed-Flash' 127 camera (Brooklyn, late 1940s). Unrelated to the Soviet FED factory despite the name; keeping it out of any Soviet FED consolidation is the point of noting this here.

name: Bell and Howell Foton
note: same camera — the 1948 Bell & Howell Foton, the American clockwork-motor rangefinder. The surviving record's Soviet-looking fixed-lens value and 1976 discontinuation are pollution from an unrelated source and are blanked in separate set rows.

name: Orionwerk Rio 14C
note: maker-prefixed duplicate of the German Orionwerk Rio 14C plate folder (1920s). Orionwerk is the pre-war German maker — unrelated to the Soviet Orion lens line or BelOMO's Orion-EE.

name: Ikkosha Co. Start 35
note: maker-prefixed duplicate of the Japanese Ikkosha Start 35 (Bolta-film viewfinder camera, ~1950). Unrelated to the KMZ Start SLR or the Polish WZFO Start TLR. The prefixed record's '35mm' format is wrong (it is a Bolta-film camera) — format pinned on the survivor in a set row.

name: Bell and Howell Autoload 342
note: maker-prefixed duplicate of the Bell & Howell (Canon-built) Autoload 342, 126 film.

name: Tair-3 300mm 1:4.5
note: same lens under the legacy ratio notation and the canonical f/N notation. Tair-3S and APO Tair-1 are genuinely distinct generations and stay separate records.

name: Start
note: the KMZ Start (1958-1964) is an interchangeable-lens SLR (its own breech bayonet, sold with a Helios-44); the 'Euktar or Emitar' fixed-lens value belongs to the Polish WZFO Start TLR — an earlier conflation of two different cameras that share a name.

name: Foton
note: the Bell & Howell Foton (introduced 1948) takes interchangeable screw-mount lenses (Taylor-Hobson Cooke Amotal standard); the 'Industar-77' fixed-lens value and the 1976 discontinuation are pollution from an unrelated (apparently Soviet) source — the Foton was a famous commercial flop dropped around 1950. Discontinuation blanked rather than guessed; the maker value had been split down to bare 'Bell'.

name: Smena 8m
note: the Smena 8M is a mass-market LOMO viewfinder camera (with the Smena-8 among the most-produced cameras ever, 21M+ units), not a toy; produced 1970-1995 (camera-wiki). The merged-in duplicate's 1965-1965 span had overwritten the discontinuation.

name: Start 35
note: pins the Bolta-film format against the merged-in duplicate's wrong '35mm' value.

name: Voskhod
note: the LOMO Voskhod has a central leaf shutter (1-1/250), not a focal-plane shutter; the merged-in duplicate record agrees (leaf).

name: Kiev 30
note: repairs the '- Industar M' junk-prefix lens name; the Kiev-30 subminiature's lens is the Industar-M 23mm f/3.5.

name: Kiev Vega
note: repairs the doubled-brand 'Industar Industar M' lens name; same Industar-M 23mm f/3.5 as the Kiev-30 that succeeded it.

name: Industar-55U
note: the Industar-55U is the BelOMO/MMZ 140mm f/4.5 enlarging lens for 9x12cm — sources agree on BelOMO/MMZ, not KMZ. It has no camera mount; the record correctly carries none.

name: Zorki 10
note: pins the clean lens value — the merged-in duplicate's doubled-brand 'Industar Industar 63' outranked the plain record's 'Industar-63' at fold time. The Zorki-10's lens is the Industar-63 45mm f/2.8.

name: Zorki 12
note: the Zorki-12 half-frame's fixed lens is the Helios-98 28mm f/2.8 — the only camera that lens ever appeared on (~7,200 units, 1967-1968).

name: Moskva-2
note: repairs the doubled-brand 'Industar Industar 23' that won the fold; the Moskva-2 6x9 folder carries the Industar-23 110mm f/4.5.

name: Moskva-5
note: repairs the doubled-brand 'Industar Industar 24'; the Moskva-5 carries the Industar-24 105mm f/3.5.

name: FT-2
note: repairs the 'Industar industar' junk name; the KMZ FT-2 swing-lens panoramic carries an Industar-50 50mm (fixed at f/5 working aperture on this body).

name: Iskra
note: normalizes the lens value; the Iskra 6x6 folder carries the Industar-58 75mm f/3.5.

name: LOMO LC-A
note: restores the plain record's correct values after the fold — the LC-A is a LOMO product (1984-2005, Russian production; Lomography's LC-A+ continued in China) with the Minitar-1 32mm f/2.8. The merged-in duplicate's GOMZ/1988-1989/'- Minitar' values had won.

name: Smena 8
note: Smena-8 production started 1963 (to 1971, then replaced by the 8M); the merged-in duplicate's 1969 intro had won the fold.

name: Smena Symbol
note: the Smena Symbol (1973-1993) is LOMO-era — GOMZ was renamed LOMO in 1965.

name: Lubitel 2
note: Lubitel-2 production started 1955; the 1949 date belongs to the original Lubitel.

name: Lubitel 166
note: the Lubitel-166 (1976-1986) is LOMO-era.

name: Lubitel 166B
note: the Lubitel-166B (1980s) is LOMO-era.

name: Agat 18
note: normalizes the lens value; the BelOMO Agat-18 half-frame carries the Industar-104 28mm f/2.8.

name: Agat 18K
note: repairs the doubled-brand 'Industar Industar 104' and blanks the 1988-1988 span's bogus discontinuation (the 18K ran from 1988 well into the 1990s; end year genuinely uncertain, so null).

name: Vilia
note: repairs the '- Triplet 69-3' junk prefix; the BelOMO Vilia (1973-1985) carries the Triplet 69-3 40mm f/4.

name: Siluet Elektro
note: repairs the '- Triplet 69-3' junk prefix; same Triplet 69-3 40mm f/4 as the Vilia.

name: Estafeta
note: repairs the '- T - 35' junk spacing; the BelOMO Estafeta's lens is the T-35 triplet.

name: Elikon 35CM
note: repairs the 'Industar -' junk left after the 35SM fold; the Elikon 35CM carries the Industar-95 38mm f/2.8.

name: Elikon Autofocus
note: repairs the doubled-brand 'Industar Industar-95'; same Industar-95 38mm f/2.8 as the 35C — autofocus is the sole difference. The 1986-1986 span's discontinuation is bogus, blanked.

name: Fed-Flash
note: repairs the '- Ultar' junk prefix on the American Federal Fed-Flash's lens name.

name: Druh
note: repairs the maker-prefixed 'WZFO Bilar' lens name.

name: Druh synchro
note: repairs the '- Bilar' junk prefix.

name: Autoload 342
note: restores the maker (split down to bare 'Bell' at fold time) and the lens spec the plain record originally carried ('Bell & Howell -' junk had won).

name: Zenit 1
note: the original Zenit is an interchangeable-lens SLR (M39 SLR thread); the Industar-22 was its kit lens, not a fixed lens.
